title: Exception handling pitfalls
context: What should you watch for when handling exceptions in Java?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java basics questions (3 of 3)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Don't catch `Exception` or `Throwable` broadly, because it hides bugs. Don't swallow an exception with an empty catch block: log it or rethrow it. Keep the original cause when wrapping, by passing it as the cause argument. Put cleanup in try-with-resources, not in `finally` blocks that can throw. Don't use exceptions for normal control flow, because creating and filling a stack trace is expensive. Don't `return` from `finally`, since it discards the exception.

points.title: Empty catch blocks
points.why: Swallowed exceptions make failures silent and hard to debug.

points.title: Keep the cause
points.why: Wrapping without the cause loses the original stack trace.

points.title: Try-with-resources
points.why: It closes resources in the right order and attaches close failures as suppressed exceptions.
